analysis:
This batch contains documentation only. It adds the changelog changelog.d/mixed-step-prefill-chunk.md (head lines 1-7) and new text in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head 549-567). Both describe the Gemma 4 mixed-step prefill geometry: 2,048-token chunks with a 4,096-token step budget. Media keeps 512-token chunks.

The docs state that KV grants, paged ring sizing (max(prefillChunkSize, soloPrefillStripeTokens)), load quotations and activation floors are unchanged. They also say the Gemma peak at eight concurrent 32k-token prompts, 3.73 GiB, stays within the 5.5 GiB default reserve. GPT-OSS and dense Qwen remain on 512/2,048 because their peaks already exceed their floors.

The security relevance is availability and memory-overcommit within TB-007 (T-029-like DoS; the UnifiedMemoryCap invariant). No consumer data path, encryption, attestation (TB-009/TB-011), authorization or prefix-cache keying (T-041) is touched. Chunk geometry does not affect cacheSalt or SSD HMAC naming as described.

The DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS overrides are operator-local. Per the changelog (line 7), using them disqualifies reviewed serving profiles. The operator is already adversarial and controls the environment under TB-003, so these overrides add no new trust grant.

Questions for integration, as implementation is not in this batch:
1. Verify that EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift usesWidePrefillChunk restricts the wide geometry to Gemma 4 and keeps media at 512.
2. Verify that paged pool sizing is truly unchanged.
3. Verify that contiguous-KV solo prompts wait or are preempted rather than overcommitting.
4. Verify that the override disqualification of reviewed profiles is enforced in code, and that `darkbloom start` forwarding is limited to these two variables.
5. Note that the docs concede the activation peak can exceed the reserve for the excluded families, even under the previous geometry. That is pre-existing and not a regression.

No regression was identified in the docs themselves.
